instruction: Find files larger than one gigabyte under the current directory, sorted largest first.
context: GNU find: -size +1G filters files above the threshold. -printf '%s %p\n' emits byte size before pathname in newline records, giving sort -n a numeric field; -r orders largest first.

instruction: Show the fifteen largest regular files anywhere below /opt, including byte counts.
context: GNU find -printf %s supplies byte size and %p supplies pathname in each record. Numeric reverse sort ranks the size field before head limits output.

instruction: Print the seven oldest .log files under /tmp with their modification timestamps.
context: GNU find -printf %T@ emits numeric modification time before %p. Ascending sort -n puts oldest records first, and head selects seven.

instruction: Sort every file path below media alphabetically without losing names containing newlines.
context: find -print0 emits NUL-delimited paths and GNU sort -z consumes the same record separator. Plain sort would instead expect newline-delimited input.

instruction: Produce null-delimited size and pathname records below backups ordered from largest to smallest.
context: find -printf terminates the complete leading-size and pathname record with \0. sort -z preserves NUL framing while -n compares size and -r reverses order.

instruction: Delete zero-byte files under scratch through xargs while handling every possible pathname.
context: find -print0 emits NUL-framed pathnames, xargs -0 consumes that framing, and -r suppresses an empty invocation. -- ends rm option parsing before paths.

instruction: Print source file paths in ordinary alphabetical line order.
context: find -print and plain sort both use newline-delimited records. No numeric ranking was requested, so filenames themselves are the lexicographic keys.

instruction: List home subdirectories by total human-readable size, largest first.
context: du -s emits one total per path and -h adds unit suffixes. sort -h understands those suffixes and -r orders largest first.
